en: A Record of Items Sent from Tang China by Great Master Jikaku to Dharma Master Ennin of the Tiantai Lotus School for His Consultations,

Including a Request for the Catalogues of the Dharma Gates, Mandalas, and Other Texts Sent [to Japan]. A Record of Items Sent from Tang China by Great Master Jikaku to Dharma Master Ennin of the Tiantai Lotus School for His Consultations, Including a Request for the Catalogues of the Dharma Gates,
Mandalas, and Other Texts Sent [to Japan].
Mahāyāna sūtras, vinayas, and śāstras;
Sanskrit and Chinese characters, mantras, ritual manuals, and hymns;
commentaries, sub-commentaries, and biographical records.
The mandalas, portraits of the Dharma-transmitting preceptors and others, and various external texts,
totaling one hundred twenty-seven works in one hundred forty-two fascicles.
The Mahāyāna sūtras, vinayas,
and śāstras comprise twelve sections in twelve fascicles,
including Sanskrit and Chinese characters, mantras, ritual manuals, and hymns.
The commentaries and biographies comprise thirty-one works in thirty-one fascicles;
the sub-commentaries and records comprise forty-nine works in sixty-three fascicles.
The diagrams of the maṇḍala altars, as well as the portraits of the Dharma-transmitters and eminent masters,
total twenty-two sections.
The external texts total fourteen works in fourteen fascicles.
Mahāyāna Sūtras, Vinayas, and Śāstras; these Mahāyāna Sūtras, Vinayas, and Śāstras combined comprise twelve divisions and twelve fascicles.

The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, one volume in eight fascicles; the *New Translation of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one volume; the *Amitābha Sūtra* (Sanskrit-Chinese Parallel Translation), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajña, one volume; the *Sarvabuddhamahāhṛdaya Sūtra*, one volume; the *Essential Collection of Dhāraṇīs* (Sanskrit-Chinese Parallel Translation), one volume; the *Mahāśrīdevī Sūtra*, one volume; the *Brief Exposition of the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions from the Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one volume; the *Subāhu-kumāra Sūtra*, one volume; the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one volume; the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one volume; and the *Method for Confessing Faults*, one volume. Furthermore, the *Commentary on the Vajracchedikā Sūtra* (Sanskrit-Chinese Parallel Translation in Verse), one volume. These twelve works, totaling twelve volumes, are contained in the same case.

Section One: *The Praise for the Ritual Manual of the Mantra of the Two-Syllable [Brahma-Chinese] Mantra*. This work consists of thirty-one sections in thirty-one fascicles, combining both Sanskrit and Chinese characters.
One fascicle of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-vidhi* in both Sanskrit and Chinese; one fascicle of the *Mahākāruṇika-nīlagrīva-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese;
one fascicle of the *Vimalaprabhā-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese; one fascicle of the *Amoghapāśa-mantra* in both Sanskrit and Chinese;
and one fascicle of the *Recitation and Offering Ritual for Akṣobhya Tathāgata* in both Sanskrit and Chinese.
One fascicle: *The Essential Yoga Method of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters).
One fascicle: *The Ritual Manual of the Great Bliss Bodhisattva Extracted Briefly from the Vajraśekhara Supreme First Yoga Sūtra* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters).
[Fragment]: *The Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters).
One fascicle of the *Sādhana-vidhi* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); one fascicle of the *Vajrasattva Samantabhadra Recitation Ritual* (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters);
one fascicle on the Fire Altar Offering and the Method for Offering to the Ten Devas (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters);

one fascicle of the Commentary on the Meaning of the Mantra of the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); and [the text on] the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa (in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters).
*The Commentary on the Meaning of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra.
*Various Miscellaneous Praises in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters*, including the *Root Praise of the Great Buddha-uṣṇīṣa*, etc., one fascicle.

*A Praise of the Compassionate Vow of Maitreya Bodhisattva after the Parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters*, one fascicle. *Twelvefold Praises in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters*, [based on] the *Lotus Sūtra*.
One fascicle titled *The Scripture on the Names of the Brahmanical Language and Various Arhats*. The above fifteen works, totaling fifteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
This is the second section of the Miscellaneous Collection.

One fascicle of the *Puxian Xingyuan Zan* (Hymn on the Vows of Samantabhadra) with Sanskrit and Chinese correspondence; one fascicle of the *Lianhua Zan* (Hymn on the Lotus) with Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
one fascicle of the *Chutan Shangfen Nianshi Yuansheng Ji Zan* (Hymn on the Recitation of the Verses on Dependent Origination for Erasing Powder from the Altar) with Sanskrit and Chinese characters;

one fascicle of the *Zuishangsheng Jiaoshou Jiehuai Wen* (Text on the Confession of Precepts according to the Highest Vehicle Instruction) with Sanskrit and Chinese characters; and one fascicle of the *Suqiu Dimu* (The Title of the Heart-Sutra) with Sanskrit and Chinese characters.
One fascicle of the *Amṛtakuṇḍalī-mahāprabhāva-dhāraṇī* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Ādigupta together with Tripiṭaka Master Jikishō;
one fascicle of the *Parṇaśavarī-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-dharma* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters;
and [one fascicle of] the *Vajradhātu-mahāmaṇḍala* in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters.
*The Secret Practice Method of Lokeśvara*, one fascicle; *The Sanskrit-Chinese Bilingual Text:
The Great Yuan Aṭavaka’s Boundless Nectar for Subjugating All Ghosts and Spirits*, one fascicle;
*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Wish-Fulfilling Wheel*, translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master; and *The Eighteen Assemblies of Vajraśekhara Yoga*.
*The Point of Return*, one fascicle; *The Essential Ritual for the Four Times of Liturgy, Offering, and Worship for Cultivating the Samādhi of Mantra*, one fascicle;
*The Separate Practice of Mudrās Extracted from the Section on the Consecration of the Tathāgata’s Great Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle;
*The Recitation Method of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *Bestowing [Relief] upon All Emaciated-Faced Hungry Ghosts*.
*The Dhāraṇī Method for Ghosts*, one fascicle; *The Siddham Chapter*, one fascicle. The above sixteen works, totaling sixteen fascicles, are bound together in this single volume.
Section Three: Miscellaneous.

The *Zhangshu Chuanji* (Records of Commentaries and Biographies) comprises forty-nine works in sixty-three fascicles. *The Meaning of the Forty-two Syllable Gates*, one fascicle, composed by the Great Master Sengzhao of Mount Nanyue.

*The Diagram of the Sequence of the Five Periods and Eight Teachings of Tiantai*, one fascicle, composed by the Great Master Zhiyi. *The Method for the Constant Practice of Samādhi*, one fascicle, composed by the Great Master Zhiyi. *The Gate of Five Expedient Means for Recollecting the Buddha*, one fascicle. *The Record of the Great Master Tiantai’s Brief Commentary on the Lotus Sūtra*, three fascicles (in three parts: upper, middle, and lower), compiled by Wang Jin, Grand Master of the Hongwen Hall. *Praise for the Amitābha Sūtra*, one fascicle, composed by the Śramaṇa Jingxia. *Commentary on the Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, four fascicles, composed by the Śramaṇa Daoli. The above seven works, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

Section Four: Miscellaneous. *Record of the Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra* in five fascicles, compiled by the śramaṇa Wengong; *Commentary on the Subtle Points of the Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra* (Guanzhong shushi wei) in two fascicles, composed by the śramaṇa Qizhen of Mount Zhongtiao; *Mirror for the Buddhist Community* (*Shimen zijing lu*) in five fascicles plus one supplementary fascicle, compiled by the monk Huixiang; and *Biographies of Miraculous Responses to the Lotus Samādhi* in two fascicles, upper and lower, composed by Dharma Master Songgu of Mount Qingliang. These four works, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Zá* (Miscellaneous), Volume 5. *Zhàolùn Chāo* (Excerpts from the *Treatise by Zhaolùn*), three fascicles; compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìchéng. *Zhàolùn Lüèchū Yàoyì* (A Brief Extraction of Essential Meanings from the *Treatise by Zhaolùn*), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Língxīng. *Zhàolùn Shū* (Commentary on the *Treatise by Zhaolùn*), one fascicle; composed by Jǔ of Dōngshān. *Zhàolùn Wénjù Tú* (Diagram of the Phrases and Sentences of the *Treatise by Zhaolùn*), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìchéng. *Dàchéng Léngqié Zhèngzōng Jué* (Decisions on the True Lineage of the Mahāyāna Laṅkāvatāra), one fascicle. *Yīnmíng Miáo Chāo* (Collected Excerpts on Logic), three fascicles; compiled by ZéLín of Zhāngjìng Temple. *Yīnmíng Rùzhèngxiàn Lùn Zuǎnyào* (Essential Compendium of the *Nyāyamukha-śāstra*), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìzhāo. *Yīnmíng Yìduàn* (Judgments on the Meaning of Logic), one fascicle; compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìzhāo. *Lìngchù Chóngqīng Yí* (Ritual for Determining the Weight of Offenses in the *Vinaya*), one fascicle; narrated by the Śramaṇa Dàoxuān. The above nine works, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
*Za* (Miscellaneous), Volume VI;

*Dabanruojingkaiti* (Introduction to the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra), one scroll; *Luejiejie* (Abridged Karmavācanā), one scroll; compiled by the śramaṇa Huaisu; *Jiezhang kewen* (Outline of the Chapter on Kalpas), one scroll;
*Shengzhe ming* (Names of the Noble Ones), one scroll; *Ershijiuwei famen* (Dharma-gate of the Twenty-nine Ranks), one scroll; *Foxing ge* (Song of Buddha-nature).
One fascicle: *A Brief Biography of Mount Qingliang*, composed by the Śramaṇa Zhenjue. One fascicle: *Record of the Great Huayan Monastery*.
One fascicle: *Epistle from the Śramaṇa Wuxing of Jingzhou*. One fascicle: *Account of Miraculous Responses*. One fascicle:

*The Pointing to the Goal of Nianfo Samādhi of Master Huizhen of Yiai Monastery on Mount Lu during the Sui Dynasty*, composed by the Śramaṇa Daoxuan. One fascicle: *Contemplating the Great...* [text fragment].

*Shi zhujing liao yi* (The Master’s Compendium on the Definitive Meaning of Various Sutras), one fascicle; *Shangdu Qingchan si zhiyan chanshi zhongchuan* (The Record of Chan Master Zhiyan of Qingchan Monastery in the Capital), one fascicle;

*Dali niu su yu seng zhiyan tongxu neifeng tan yan fashi tan qi ge bing wen* (Record of Niu Su of Dali, Together with Monk Zhiyan, Narrating the Discourse of the Inner Offering Master Tanyan and Praising Qi Ge), one fascicle;
*Tan qi wen* (Texts Praising Qi), five fascicles; *Fu* (Supplement), one fascicle. The above total consists of fourteen works in ten fascicles.
Four fascicles in one volume.
Section Seven: Miscellaneous.
One scroll of Master Tiantai’s *Contemplating the Mind while Reciting Sutras*; one scroll of the *Karmavācanā* by Master Nanyue Huisi.
One fascicle of the *Dharmaparyāya Transmission*, written by the lay disciple Weiwei Cheng Du Fei; one fascicle of the *Record of Śākyamuni Tathāgata’s Worthy Kalpa*;
one fascicle of the *Internal Biography of the Buddha*; one fascicle of the "Homage to the Triple Gem" along with the introductory preface and colophon;
one fascicle of the *Resolution on the Cultivation and Realization of Samādhi through Holding the Lotus Sūtra*; and one [fascicle] of the "Text for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts."
One fascicle: "Eulogy on the Virtues of the Sangha Rectifier" by Tie; one fascicle: "Commentary on the Eulogy of the Kalpa Chapter"; one fascicle:
"Record of the Eulogy of the Kalpa Chapter" compiled by the Śramaṇa Bianzhi; ten fascicles: "Baolin Zhuan of Caoqi" composed by the Śramaṇa Daoquan;
two fascicles: "Stele for Master Yan of Dongdayun Monastery in Yangzhou"; one fascicle: "The Hells of All Heavens and Earths."
One fascicle of verses on the *Lotus Sūtra* in seven-character lines concerning the limits of the lifespan, totaling fifty-seven stanzas in one fascicle;
the above sixteen works in seventeen fascicles are contained in the same volume,
Miscellaneous Volume VIII.
The mandala altar designs and the transmission dharma and superior shadow mandala altar designs, totaling twenty-two sets.
One set of three scrolls of the Great Vairocana Great Compassion Womb Matrix (Mahākaruṇā-garbha) Great Maṇḍala;
one set of seven scrolls of the Vajradhātu Great Maṇḍala; one set of the Vajradhātu Seed-Syllable Maṇḍala of Eighty-One Deities;
one set of the Vajradhātu Seed-Syllable Maṇḍala of Thirty-Seven Deities; and the Vajradhātu [Maṇḍala].
One scroll of the *Tāra* iconography; one scroll of the *Lotus Sūtra Maṇḍala* iconography; one scroll of the Avalokiteśvara altar layout;
one scroll of the image of the Bodhisattva Vajramukha-Śūkaramukha; one scroll of the image of the Bodhisattva Vajramukha;
one set of three scrolls depicting the portrait of Master Zhiyi of Mount Nanyue; one set [of scrolls] depicting the portrait of Master Zhiyi of Tiantai.
Three scrolls: a portrait of the Saṃgha Upādhyāya; one portrait of Meditation Master Deng of Liangtishan; one image of an Araṇyaka Bhikṣu;
one portrait of Meditation Master Ying of Jiangyang Yongqi Temple from the Sui dynasty; one portrait of Meditation Master Huixiang;
one portrait of Meditation Master Fahui of the Liang dynasty; and one portrait of Meditation Master Huibin of the Sui dynasty.
One portrait of Master Ding Chan of the Jiangyang Chanzong Temple; one portrait of Master Daochao of Qijun;
one portrait of an elder monk of Dongsi in Qinjun; and one portrait of Master Fahui of Quishui Temple in Chen.
The above twenty-two scrolls are contained within one lacquered wooden chest with a clay seal.
The "External Writings" (Wàishū) consist of fourteen works in fourteen fascicles. They are: one letter containing poems exchanged between those of Hangzhou and Yuezhou along with their prefaces;

one letter containing new poems by the śramaṇa Qingjiang; one letter of judicial decisions totaling one hundred items; one letter on the ritual of formal audience; one letter titled "Lament for Lady Rén"; one letter by Bái Jǐyì on chrysanthemums in winter; one letter titled "Grasping Lètiān’s Writing"; one letter titled "Eulogy of Virtue"; one letter of miscellaneous poems; one letter of poetry addressed to Yuán Yīng; one letter of miscellaneous poems; one scroll of poetry by the former jinshi Chǐ Jiānwú; one scroll of "Extended Discourse in the Han Language" (Hányǔ Chángyán); and one scroll of "Human Figures of the Persian People. These fourteen works in fourteen fascicles are contained in the same volume.
Miscellaneous, No. 9.
Separate items, separate items, sealed leather boxes, one set of cases.
A letter from the Dharma Master Yuanren requesting instruction. Written by Ni.
One fascicle of the *Prajñā-naya-vyākhyāna-sūtra*.
The *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in Sanskrit characters. The Sanskrit manuscript of the *Bhagavatī-prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra*.
Verses on the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in Sanskrit characters;
miscellaneous Sanskrit names;
seventeen altar layouts.
The layout of the homa altar;
the hand gestures (mudrā) of the Womb Realm (Garbhadhātu);
and the ritual procedures for the five secrets, etc.
He took a chest and filled it completely,
sealing it so that it could not be opened,
for a certain reason.
This is not for one who begrudges the Dharma-gate.
The above was written by Ennin at the request of the Dharma Master Chuandeng, who holds the rank of Yuanren.
Furthermore, regarding the newly translated and compiled Dharma-gates that I have sought out:
Along with the two mandalas and other items,
these were sent to Enryaku-ji.
This included all the mantra ritual manuals and so forth.
Tang Guohe and others were especially cautioned against this;
one must not scatter [the offerings] recklessly.
However, its catalog was previously attached to the second ship.
As for the clerk Sotada, he has nonetheless recorded it as follows.
The nineteenth day of the first month in the seventh year of the Jōwa era.
The *Dūvina* (Chief Administrative Officer), the monk Jinenzen, who holds the rank of *Denpō Jūi*;
and the *Jishu* (Abbot), the monk Chijaku, who holds the rank of *Denpō Jūi*.
The Elder Dharma-lamp, the monk who occupies the station [of authority], Eido.
